Thousands who left their homes fearing death were told by Allah to die and were then restored to life, yet most people do not show gratitude.
A man who asked how a ruined town could live again is made to die a hundred years and revived, and Abraham is shown how Allah revives the dead.
They say there is only worldly life and no resurrection, yet before their Lord they will admit the truth, taste punishment, and regret when the Hour comes suddenly.
All return to Allah; He begins creation and repeats it to reward justly those who believed and did righteous deeds, while disbelievers get scalding water and painful punishment.
Asked if resurrection is true, the Prophet swears it is; wrongdoers would offer all on earth as ransom; Allah owns all, gives life and death, and all return to Him.
They ask whether, once dust, they will be a new creation; those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, with shackles on their necks, abiding in the Fire.
Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth; if He wills He can do away with people and bring a new creation, and that is not difficult for Him.
They swear Allah will not raise the dead, but it is His true promise, to show them what they differed over; He says to a thing Be, and it is.
They ask whether bones and dust will be raised as a new creation; whatever they become, He who first made them will restore them, perhaps soon.
Allah, who created the heavens and earth, can create their like and has set them a sure term, yet the wrongdoers refuse all but disbelief.
The disbeliever asks if he will be raised alive after death, forgetting that Allah created him before when he was nothing.
Doubters of the Resurrection are reminded of their creation from dust in stages and barren earth revived by rain; Allah revives the dead and will raise those in graves.
Like former peoples, they ask whether they will be resurrected after becoming dust and bones, calling the promise legends of the former peoples.
Only Allah knows the unseen; people do not perceive when they will be resurrected and doubt the Hereafter, and disbelievers call being brought out after becoming dust old legends.
Allah begins creation and repeats it, which is easy for Him; He punishes or shows mercy as He wills, none escapes Him, and deniers of meeting Him despair of mercy.
Allah begins creation, then repeats it, and to Him all will be returned.
Allah brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living and revives the lifeless earth, and so will people be brought out.
Creating and resurrecting all people is, for Allah, like doing so for a single soul.
Disbelievers ask if they will be created anew after being lost in the earth; the angel of death will take them, and then they return to their Lord.
Disbelievers ask whether the man who tells of new creation after disintegration has invented a lie about Allah or is mad, though Allah could make the earth swallow them.
Allah sends winds that drive clouds to dead land and revive the earth after its lifelessness, and so is the resurrection.
Allah brings the dead to life and records what they sent ahead and left behind, with all things counted in a clear register.
When the Horn is blown they hasten from their graves, asking who raised them, and with one blast all are brought before Allah, where no soul is wronged.
Man, made from a sperm-drop, asks who will give life to disintegrated bones; He who made them the first time will, for He need only say Be, and it is.
Mocking signs as magic, disbelievers ask whether they and their forefathers will be raised after becoming dust and bones; yes, they will be made contemptible, raised by one shout.
The creation of the heavens and earth is greater than the creation of mankind, so recreating people is easy for Allah, but most people do not know.
These people say there is only the first death and no resurrection, demanding their forefathers back; yet the people of Tubba' and those before them were destroyed as criminals.
They say there is only worldly life and time destroys them, and demand their forefathers back; Allah gives life and death and will assemble them for the Day of Resurrection.
Allah, who created the heavens and earth without failing, can give life to the dead, and disbelievers exposed to the Fire will confess it is the truth.
By the honored Quran, the disbelievers wonder at a warner from among them and reject returning after becoming dust, though Allah knows what the earth takes of them.
Allah did not fail in the first creation, yet they are in confusion over a new creation.
On the Day the Caller calls and the blast is heard, people emerge from the earth swiftly; Allah gives life and death, and this gathering is easy for Him.
The Prophet is to leave them; when the Caller calls, they will emerge from graves like spreading locusts, racing to him, and disbelievers will call it a difficult Day.
Allah, who created people from the fluid they emit and decreed death among them, can recreate them in a form they do not know, as the first creation shows.
Disbelievers claim they will never be resurrected, but they surely will be and will be told what they did, so believe in Allah, His Messenger and the Quran.
By the Day of Resurrection and the reproaching soul, Allah can reassemble man's bones, even his fingertips, yet man wants to keep sinning and asks when that Day is.
Man will not be left neglected; Allah, who formed him from a drop of semen and a clot into male and female, is able to give life to the dead.
They ask whether they will be returned to life after becoming decayed bones, calling it a losing return, yet one shout will bring them onto the earth's surface.
Man is cursed for disbelief; Allah created him from a sperm-drop, eased his way, causes his death and burial and will raise him, yet he has not fulfilled His command.
By the sky and the piercing star, every soul has a protector; Allah can return man, created from an ejected fluid, on the Day secrets are put on trial.
